title: Checkpoint: Decline and Conquest
objective: After this level you can explain how Egypt passed from pharaohs to foreign rulers.
summary: After the New Kingdom, Egypt split and then passed through Kushite, Persian, Macedonian Greek, Roman and Arab hands. Most conquerors ruled as pharaohs, until new faiths closed the temples.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: how Egypt passed from pharaohs to foreign rulers.
cards.body: You’ve met raiders, priest-kings, Kushites, Persians, Alexander, the Ptolemies, Rome and new faiths. Here’s how they fit together.

events.label: Ramesses III beats off the Sea Peoples
Kush takes Egypt; the 25th Dynasty rules
Egypt becomes a province of Rome

cards.headline: One story
cards.body: Egypt beat the Sea Peoples and still came out weaker. It split between kings at Tanis and priests at Thebes, and outsiders stepped in: Kushites who worshipped Amun, a Persian crowned pharaoh, Alexander greeted as son of Amun, Ptolemies carved as pharaohs, Romans who shipped its grain home. Native kings returned only once, and Nectanebo II was the last. Libraries faded slowly and temples closed. The crown kept changing heads; the land kept feeding whoever wore it.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: How Egypt passed from native pharaohs to Kushite, Persian, Greek, Roman and Arab rule.
Why most foreign conquerors chose to present themselves as pharaohs.
Why Egypt mattered so much to Rome, which fed its people on Nile-grown grain.
How Christianity and later Islam slowly replaced the old gods, temple by temple.

questions.prompt: Decline and Conquest recap: which of these foreign powers ruled Egypt first?

options.label: Persia
options.rationale: Persia came in 525 BCE, after Kush.

options.label: Rome
options.rationale: Rome came last of these, in 30 BCE.

options.label: The Macedonian Ptolemies
options.rationale: They came after Alexander, in the 4th century BCE.

questions.explanation: Kush conquered Egypt in the 8th century BCE, before Persia (525 BCE), the Ptolemies and Rome (30 BCE).

questions.prompt: Decline and Conquest recap: who was the last native Egyptian king?

options.label: Ramesses III
options.rationale: He fought the Sea Peoples, centuries earlier.

options.label: Herihor
options.rationale: He was a priest-king at Thebes, long before.

options.label: Amyrtaeus of Sais
options.rationale: He began the last spell of native rule in 404 BCE.

questions.explanation: Nectanebo II reigned until Persia reconquered Egypt in 343 BCE; he was the last native king.

questions.prompt: Decline and Conquest recap: why didn’t Ramesses III’s victory over the Sea Peoples keep the New Kingdom strong?

options.label: The Sea Peoples came back and conquered Egypt
The wider region collapsed, and Egypt came out much diminished
Ramesses III handed Egypt to the Hittites
Rome invaded soon after the battle
options.rationale: Rome took Egypt over a thousand years later.

questions.explanation: Egypt was the only major power to resist, but in the Late Bronze Age collapse it lost much of its influence and power.

questions.prompt: Decline and Conquest recap: what did Cambyses II, Alexander and the Ptolemies have in common in Egypt?

options.label: They all came from the kingdom of Kush
They all moved Egypt’s capital to Tanis
options.rationale: Tanis was a Third Intermediate Period capital.

options.label: They all presented themselves as pharaohs
They all shut down Egypt’s temples
options.rationale: The temples closed later, under Christian emperors.

questions.explanation: Cambyses was crowned pharaoh, Alexander wore the double crown, and the Ptolemies appeared as pharaohs on temple walls.

questions.prompt: Decline and Conquest recap: the Kushite kings and Alexander both honored the same Egyptian god. Which one?

options.label: Serapis
options.rationale: Serapis was promoted later, by Ptolemy I.

options.label: Isis
options.rationale: Her temple at Philae appears in Level 89.

options.label: Apis
options.rationale: Alexander honored Apis, but Kush’s god was Amun.

questions.explanation: Amun’s cult was strongly rooted in Kush, and at Siwa Alexander was greeted as son of Amun.
